title: GT Frobenius-orbit square-and-add rho with bounded Floyd detection, hardened v4 (fixed-G2 invert-G1)

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in BLS12-381 G2, uniform z in GT and fresh algorithm coins, compute g=e(P0,Q), solve z=g^x by the concrete Frobenius-class square-and-add walk in argument.md, and return P=[x]P0 for that exact supplied Q. The analytic claim is total classical work at most 2^(6441/50)=2^128.82 dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents at fixed C=20000, with success at least 0.39 under the explicitly disclosed production random-mapping transfer assumption Hmix and exceptional-key assumption Hkey. The comparison model has success greater than 0.4647, or greater than 0.432 after a 5-percent walk-length slowdown, not a measured production success rate. One bounded Floyd tortoise/hare run detects its own class cycles without restart counters or escape ladders; each iteration costs three square-and-add evaluations, six dense products. The nominal scored envelope is 8*T+2^100, whose log2 is between 128.7977 and 128.7978; the claim is 0.0222 to 0.0223 bits above that envelope. The 1.2-times repricing of every nonreference executed-work ceiling is below 2^128.694 and leaves over 0.126 bits below the claim. Auxiliary distinguished-point storage is optional for success and has a hard 2^69-record limit per generation, 129 generations, 128-byte records and peak memory below 2^78 bytes; its 128-bit fingerprint is disjoint from all fixed DP bits. Candidate verification, overflow, setup, randomness, pairings and output are charged; preprocessing is at most 2^50 equivalents within the total, and nonuniform advice is zero bytes. This is an exploratory analytic upper-bound construction, not a production attack or an improvement over the public 125.89 prior-work claim. The certificate checks exact integer/rational arithmetic only; captured toy experiments support mechanisms at their stated scale, not production mixing or instruction measurements.
